question: Compare the quantitative triggers in the four-leg All-Way Stop crash warrant and the 8-hour volume warrant.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The two All-Way Stop Control warrants use different kinds of quantitative triggers. The crash warrant (Warrant A) for a four-leg intersection is triggered by crash frequency — five or more reported crashes in 12 months, or six or more in 36 months, of a type correctable by all-way stop control. The 8-hour volume warrant (Warrant D) is triggered by traffic volume — at least 300 combined units per hour entering from the major-street approaches and at least 200 units per hour from the minor-street approaches, for each of the same 8 hours of a typical day. Both are Option provisions requiring an engineering study. Options (permitted): - Crash warrant (four-leg): "All-way stop control may be installed at an intersection where an engineering study indicates that: A. For a four-leg intersection, there are five or more reported crashes in a 12-month period or six or more reported crashes in a 36-month period that were of a type susceptible to correction by the installation of all-way stop control." - 8-hour volume warrant: "All-way stop control may be installed at an intersection where an engineering study indicates: A. The combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the major-street approaches is at least 300 units per hour for each of any 8 hours of a typical day; and B. The combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volume entering the intersection from the minor-street approaches is at least 200 units per hour for each of any of the same 8 hours." Comparison of the quantitative triggers: - Metric type: Warrant A counts reported crashes of a correctable type; Warrant D counts combined motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian volumes (in "units per hour"). - Thresholds: Warrant A (four-leg) — ≥5 crashes/12 months OR ≥6 crashes/36 months. Warrant D — ≥300 units/hour (major-street approaches) AND ≥200 units/hour (minor-street approaches). - Time basis: Warrant A uses a retrospective crash history window (12 or 36 months, satisfied by either alternative). Warrant D uses any 8 hours of a typical day, and both the major- and minor-street conditions must be met during the same 8 hours (an AND condition, unlike Warrant A's OR condition). Citations: - Section 2B.13 Option §1 (p.79) - Section 2B.16 Option §1 (p.79)
gold_answer: The crash warrant may apply with at least 5 correctable crashes in 12 months or 6 in 36 months. The volume warrant may apply when, for the same 8 hours, major-street entering volume is at least 300 units/hour and minor-street entering volume at least 200 units/hour, with a possible 70-percent adjustment if major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph.
